# routeros_app (Resource)


## Example Usage
```terraform
resource "routeros_app" "app" {
  auto_update             = true
  container_command_lines = "example"
  devices                 = "example"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `___id___` (Number) <em>Resource ID type (.id / name). This is an internal service field, setting a value is not required.</em>
- `___path___` (String) <em>Resource path for CRUD operations. This is an internal service field, setting a value is not required.</em>
- `___skip___` (String) <em>A set of transformations for field names. This is an internal service field, setting a value is not required.</em>
- `auto_update` (Boolean) Whether this application is updated automatically when a new container image is published. Overrides the global `/app/settings` value.
- `container_command_lines` (String) Comma separated list of `container:command:image` entries overriding the command line and the image of the individual containers of the application.
- `devices` (String) Comma separated list of host devices that are passed through to the containers of the application, for example a PCI address, `serial0` or a disk name.
- `disabled` (Boolean)
- `environment` (String) Comma separated list of `container:VARIABLE=value` entries passed to the containers of the application as environment variables.
- `extra_mounts` (String) Comma separated list of additional mounts attached to the containers of the application.
- `firewall_redirects` (String) Comma separated list of `router-port:container-port:protocol:container` entries that redirect traffic from the router to the application.
- `network` (String) Network the application is attached to:
  * default - the network requested by the YAML document of the application,
  * internal - an isolated network behind NAT,
  * lan - the bridge configured as `lan_bridge` in `/app/settings`,
  * the name of a bridge.
- `network_outgoing_access` (Boolean) Whether the application may open outgoing connections. When disabled RouterOS adds a mangle drop rule for its traffic.
- `network_pvid` (Number) Port VLAN ID of the veth interface of the application in the bridge.
- `required_hw_devices` (String) Comma separated list of hardware devices that must be present before the application is allowed to start.
- `required_mounts` (String) Comma separated list of mounts that must be available before the application is allowed to start.
- `secrets` (String, Sensitive) Comma separated list of `app__secret:=value` entries holding the secrets the application asks for, such as generated administrator passwords.
- `use_https` (Boolean) Whether the URLs of the application use HTTPS with the certificate reported by `/app/settings`.
- `yaml` (String) The YAML document describing the application: its name, description, the containers it consists of, the mounts and the RouterOS configuration it needs.

### Read-Only

- `app_store_url` (String) URL of the app store entry the application was installed from.
- `category` (String) Category the application declares in its YAML document, used for grouping in WebFig.
- `custom` (Boolean) Whether the application was defined locally instead of being taken from an app store.
- `default_network` (String) Network the YAML document of the application asks for, used when `network=default`.
- `description` (String) Description taken from the YAML document of the application.
- `from_app_store` (Boolean) Whether the application was installed from an app store.
- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `interface` (String) Name of the veth interface RouterOS created for the application.
- `ip_address` (String) Address assigned to the application on the selected network.
- `name` (String) Name of the application. It is taken from the `name` field of the YAML document and cannot be set separately.
- `project_page` (String) Home page of the project, taken from the YAML document of the application.
- `running` (Boolean)
- `ui_url` (String) URL of the web interface of the application, when it provides one.

## Import
Import is supported using the following syntax:
```shell
#The ID can be found via API or the terminal
#The command for the terminal is -> :put [/app get [print show-ids]]
terraform import routeros_app.app "*1"
```
